ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Jane Austen — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Seven-month review: replacement, renin, thyroid, mood, and the closing of the differential

text.paragraph: Seven-month review: replacement, renin, thyroid, mood, and the closing of the differential. [S]

Ms. Austen returns seven months after diagnosis. She feels well. She writes every morning and walks several miles most days, and she has had no illness needing stress doses since the spring. She has had no fevers, night sweats or lumps. Her back has given her scarcely any pain for months. Her periods are regular. She notices that the darkness of her hands has nearly gone. She carries her kit and wears her medical ID. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1816-10-12; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Faint residual pigmentation of the palmar creases and gums; no thin skin, striae, bruising or facial rounding
No cervical, supraclavicular, axillary or inguinal nodes

About three months of increasing tiredness, loss of 5 kg, darkening of the skin, nausea with bouts of vomiting, low back ache, salt craving and lightheadedness on standing, with low sodium, high potassium and raised eosinophils; adrenal insufficiency suspected and urgent endocrinology testing booked
S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis at the consultation; its timing echoes the documented break in her health (D).

Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease): no cortisol response to cosyntropin with a markedly raised ACTH, and mineralocorticoid deficiency with raised renin and low aldosterone; on hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone; synthetic modern diagnosis chosen for a historical illness whose cause is disputed
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the historical cause of her illness remains undetermined (R, disputed).
Mild normocytic anemia (hemoglobin 11.4 g/dL) with normal ferritin, vitamin B12 and folate
S — Synthetic finding at intake; it recovers on replacement.
Group A streptococcal pharyngitis with fever, treated with amoxicillin and doubled hydrocortisone under the sick-day rules; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Primary adrenal insufficiency (autoimmune Addison's disease) (E27.1). Well replaced: weight back to her usual 57 kg, pigmentation nearly gone, no postural drop, sodium 140 and potassium 4.2 mmol/L, plasma renin activity 2.8 ng/mL/h. TSH 2.9 mIU/L, normal. The differential can be closed: the positive antibodies explain the illness, and with full recovery of weight and energy, no fevers or night sweats, no nodes or enlarged spleen, a normal LDH and a normal chest X-ray at diagnosis, nothing suggests lymphoma, so no CT is needed. [S]
Continue current doses.
Electrolytes, renin and TSH yearly; vitamin B12, A1c and celiac serology at one year.
Endocrinology review at one year.
Influenza vaccine and the second hepatitis B dose today.

list.item: A diagnosis within one week of the first visit, with treatment started the same day if adrenal insufficiency is confirmed. Outcome by 1816-03-19: Cosyntropin test three days after the first visit; replacement started the same day [S]
No adrenal crisis and no emergency admission through the episode. Outcome by 1816-10-12: No crisis or admission; one febrile illness managed at home with stress dosing [S]

Sodium and potassium normal, renin in the upper normal range, and no postural drop by the six-week visit. Outcome by 1816-04-30: Sodium 139 and potassium 4.4 mmol/L; renin 3.4 ng/mL/h; no postural drop [S]
She can state the sick-day rules and give the emergency injection by the two-week visit. Outcome by 1816-04-02: Stated the rules and gave a practice injection on a trainer [S]
Weight back to her usual 57 kg, and energy for full mornings of writing, by six months. Outcome by 1816-10-12: Weight 57.2 kg from 52.0; writing full mornings and walking several miles [S]

Follow-up: Endocrinology review in five months, with vitamin B12, A1c and celiac serology at one year. Primary care review every six months, with electrolytes, renin and TSH yearly. Follow the sick-day rules for any illness. [S]
